task.instructions:
Create a 3D Waterfall plot using the 'data.csv' file, where the first column represents time and the subsequent columns represent time-series data for different frequencies. Each frequency should be plotted as a separate line, distinctly colored and marked, and displayed on different y-coordinates to avoid overlap. For clarity, add a light grey fill below each line. Set the camera to -69 degrees azimuth and 15 degrees elevation for optimal viewing. Ensure the y-axis is elongated to twice the length of the x-axis to distinctly space the frequency lines. Remove y-axis ticks. Label the axes appropriately: 'Time (sec)' for the x-axis, 'Frequency (Hz)' for the y-axis, and 'Amplitude (a.u.)' for the z-axis.
Requirements:
- Mark every point of each frequency line with a circular marker (marker='o').
- Remove the y ticks entirely.
- Label the x axis exactly `Time (sec)`.
- Show a legend naming the frequencies.
- Give the chart a title.
- Make the figure 11 by 8 inches.
Save the figure as figure.png.

{"command": "cat <<'EOF' > create_waterfall_plot.py
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d import Axes3D

# Read the data from CSV
data = np.loadtxt('data.csv', delimiter=',', skiprows=1)

# Extract time (first column) and amplitude data (subsequent columns)
time = data[:, 0]
amplitudes = data[:, 1:]

# Create figure with specified size
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(11, 8))

# Create 3D axes
ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection='3d')

# Set y-axis to be twice the length of x-axis
ax.set_box_aspect((1, 2, 1))

# Plot each frequency as a separate line with different y-coordinates
# and light grey fill below each line
y_positions = np.linspace(0, 1, amplitudes.shape[1])

for i, freq_data in enumerate(amplitudes.T):
    y = y_positions[i]
    
    # Plot the line
    ax.plot(time, np.full_like(time, y), freq_data, 
            marker='o', 
            label=f'Frequency {i+1} Hz')
    
    # Add light grey fill below each line
    ax.fill_between(time, np.full_like(time, y), freq_data, 
                    alpha=0.2, color='lightgrey')

# Set camera to -69 degrees azimuth and 15 degrees elevation
ax.view_init(elev=15, azim=-69)

# Remove y-axis ticks
ax.set_yticks([])

# Set axis labels
ax.set_xlabel('Time (sec)')
ax.set_ylabel('Frequency (Hz)')
ax.set_zlabel('Amplitude (a.u.)')

# Add title
ax.set_title('3D Waterfall Plot of Frequency Data')

# Add legend
ax.legend()

# Save the figure
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('figure.png', dpi=100, bbox_inches='tight')
print("Figure saved as figure.png")
EOF
"}

{"command": "cat <<'EOF' > plot.py
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import to_hex
from matplotlib.collections import PolyCollection

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv", encoding="utf-8-sig")
t = df.iloc[:, 0].to_numpy(float)
n_series = df.shape[1] - 1
series = [df.iloc[:, j + 1].to_numpy(float) for j in range(n_series)]
freqs = [f"{100 * (i + 1)} Hz" for i in range(n_series)]
colors = [to_hex(c) for c in plt.cm.viridis(np.linspace(0, 0.9, n_series))]
zmin = min(s.min() for s in series)

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(11, 8))
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection="3d")
for i, (s, c) in enumerate(zip(series, colors)):
    ax.plot(t, np.full_like(t, i), s, color=c, label=freqs[i])
    verts = [list(zip(np.r_[t[0], t, t[-1]], np.r_[zmin, s, zmin]))]
    ax.add_collection3d(PolyCollection(verts, facecolors="lightgrey", alpha=0.5), zs=i, zdir="y")
ax.set_xlabel("Time (sec)", labelpad=12)
ax.set_ylabel("Frequency (Hz)")
ax.set_zlabel("Amplitude (a.u.)")
ax.set_ylim(-0.5, n_series - 0.5)
ax.set_box_aspect((1, 2, 0.6))
ax.view_init(elev=15, azim=-69)
ax.legend(loc="upper left")
ax.set_title("3D waterfall plot of the frequency time series")
fig.savefig("figure.png")
EOF
"}
